recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants stronger delivery guarantees or more prescriptive delta semantics, that should be handled as new work; FHIR-19976 itself is already reflected in current source.
issue_request: FHIR-19976 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Subscription request to clarify that subscribers cannot assume every data update, delete, authorization change, or subscription/filter change will result in a notification. The approved resolution was to add clarifying examples adjusted for the R5 Subscription redesign.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit ba1ecb7480d6a0776e6bd122a489a84899b29aa1, which added security/privacy notification-generation guidance and refined the delivery limitation caveat in source/subscriptions.html. The R5 redesign context in FHIR-23738 also listed FHIR-19976 as covered by the redesigned SubscriptionTopic-based approach.
additional_context: The linked Zulip discussion raised updates or deletes that make resources stop qualifying, referenced-list/filter complications, and authorization changes. FHIR-I minutes approved clarifying examples adjusted for the revamped design. Later Applied R6 issues FHIR-43516 and FHIR-47280 preserved or reorganized the limitation guidance without reversing it.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source keeps Subscription active in the build, points Subscription readers to the Subscriptions Framework page, and the framework page explains authorization checks, security/privacy suppression of notification generation, implementation-specific cases where notifications SHOULD NOT be sent, and best-effort delivery limitations.

related_jiras.note: The broader R5 topic-based Subscription redesign explicitly listed FHIR-19976 as covered by the redesigned safety text and server-advertised SubscriptionTopics.
This Applied R6 issue addressed duplicate notification-limitation wording and preserved the guidance rather than changing its meaning.
This Applied R6 terminology/disambiguation refactor retained the Safety and Security and Scoping Responsibilities guidance relevant to FHIR-19976.
